kjv: thou (David) hast given great occasion to the enemies of the LORD to blaspheme
note: The MT reads ni'ets ni'atsta 'et-'oyevei YHWH ("you have utterly scorned the enemies of Yahweh"). "Enemies" is widely regarded as a pious scribal buffer, as in 1 Sam 25:22, to avoid saying David scorned God. The KJV keeps "enemies" and expands the verb to "given occasion to blaspheme". I removed the buffer.

kjv: put them (the people of Rabbah) under saws, and under harrows of iron ... and made them pass through the brickkiln
mine: set them (the people of Rabbah) to labor with saws and iron picks and iron axes and made them toil at the brick kilns
note: wayyasem bammegerah means "put them to (work with) the saw". he'evir bammalben (qere) means "made them work at the brick-mould". The KJV reads it as torture (being sawn and burned), which would be atrocity. The Hebrew more naturally describes forced labour.
